context.objective: Document how we carry out Carry Vesting & Carry Point Reallocation, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: When a partner's carry changes, the preparer opens a change record from the GP-02 package, checks the governing terms and any approved exception, then ties the prior points and carry to the workbook. The client chooses the allowed method and names recipients. If they select Method B, we put it on hold. We never run Method B from this procedure.
What does the preparer compare to confirm the prior points and carry tie to the workbook?

We compare the prior schedules, workbooks, distributions and amounts recorded. Original points, cumulative allocations and distributions and the carry calculation base must tie. Next we verify the governing vested percentage and any approved exception, calculate vested and released points and allocate all released points to named recipients. Total member point changes must equal zero. The rounding rule and threshold for action remain unconfirmed.
After the total member point changes are confirmed to equal zero, what happens next in the process?

We keep the old schedule, build a new dated schedule, include approved deals or tranches, verify coverage of periods and tie the totals. Under go-forward treatment earlier amounts stay unchanged. We use the approved schedule from its effective date, calculate carry from inception through the current period and subtract what's already recorded. A reviewer checks governing support, computations, entries and outputs before final schedules are protected and sent to GP-01 and GP-06. The final release role is unconfirmed.
When Method B is selected and the work is put on hold, what happens to the change next?

Document the selection and the hold. GP03-GAP-02 blocks calculation, posting, withholding, offsets and release of Method B. Only a concept exists; the formula, tests, release criteria and approvals require the process owner, Accounting, client and relevant Legal or Tax input. I cannot tell you the executable formula or that anyone has approved it.
What can go wrong if a vesting or point-reallocation error reaches the final schedules?

The wrong recipient, vested percentage or effective date can change cumulative allocations, the current entry and downstream GP-01/GP-06 outputs. The preparer ties the starting position, proves total point changes are zero and checks periods and totals; a reviewer checks the package before release. The authority to correct and reissue outputs and the named release approver still need confirmation.
When a check fails, what happens to the schedules or calculations before they can be released?

We hold the change if governing support, recipient allocation, total points or schedules fail validation. Preserve prior schedules, resolve the underlying error with approved support, repeat the proof and submit a complete package with no blocking hold for review. I can't name the correction or release authority from this procedure.
How does the preparer typically learn that a partner’s carry has changed?
